 "old_content": "# Full-coverage audit verdict — PR #116 must not merge yet\n\n- **Audited target:** `madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn` @ `7b832d61c183f138a5db8b5bef1806f6288d8b73`\n- **PR under review:** #116 `feat/full-coverage-audit` @ `685026b3` (draft, base `main`)\n- **Run evidence:** Actions run `39074720296` (full), `39075485016` (sampled control on the PR branch),\n  `39075692475` (sampled control on `main`), `38790744542` (pre-change full run on `main`)\n- **Verdict:** the sweep and its coverage ledger are correct and worth keeping. The shared\n  routing policy bundled into the same PR is **not** safe to merge as written.\n- **No writes were made to the target, no branches were created on the target, no target code\n  was executed.** All actions were read-only plus a local, throwaway `freelm` probe.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Acceptance test and result\n\nThe merge rule set for this work was explicit:\n\n> If the report shows `Files examined: N/N (100%)` and every chunk answered, merge #116.\n> If any chunk failed, send me the report and we'll see why before merging.\n\nObserved result of the full run (`39074720296`, 2026-10-17):\n\n```\nStatus: COMPLETED | 47 finding(s); 2 contradicted; examined 72/100 files (72%)\n- Files examined: 72/100 (72%)\n- Chunks: 21/29 answered\n- Failed chunks: 8 of 29\n- Route: kilo / nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free\n```\n\n**72%, not 100%. Eight chunks failed.** The acceptance condition was not met, so #116 was\nnot merged and no branch was pushed to the target.\n\nThe failure mode is identical in all eight chunks. From the run artifact\n(`company-audit-full.json` → `chunkNotes`):\n\n| Chunk | Files | Note |\n|-------|-------|------|\n| chunk-4  | 1 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-10 | 1 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-16 | 3 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-17 | 2 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-19 | 2 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-20 | 7 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-24 | 4 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-27 | 8 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n\nThe 26 files never examined include `src/company/model.ts`, `src/company/evidence.ts`,\n`src/company/registry.ts`, `src/company/deliver.ts`, `src/company/judge.ts`,\n`src/company/roles.ts`, `src/agent/tools.ts`, and 12 test files — that is, most of the\nengine this PR touches.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Correction to an earlier claim\n\nAn earlier analysis asserted that `freelm` gives keyless endpoints `priority: 100` meaning\nthey are tried **first**, and described the routing change as a \"priority inversion\".\n**That claim was wrong and is withdrawn.** The ordering was measured directly rather than\ninferred from reading minified code:\n\n```\nkeyless:true -> google(p=0) , groq(p=0) , kilo(p=100) , ovh(p=100)\nkeyless:auto -> google(p=0) , groq(p=0)\n```\n\nLower number wins. Keyed providers sort **first**; the anonymous keyless endpoints sort\n**last**. The premise stated in #116 — that keyless is a genuine last resort — is correct.\n\nWhat follows is the mechanism that actually holds, established by test, not by reading.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Root cause\n\nThe defect is not ordering. It is **pool membership**.\n\nOn `main`, hard-tier work used:\n\n```ts\nkeyless: hasProviderKeys ? 'auto' : true,   // keyed-only pool when keys exist\n```\n\n#116 replaced this for every tier with:\n\n```ts\nkeyless: keylessOption(this.env),           // always true\n```\n\n`'auto'` builds a keyed-only pool when keys are present. `true` **always appends** the\nanonymous Kilo/OVHcloud routes to the pool. A controlled probe of what that changes when a\nkeyed free tier is rate-limited (`429`):\n\n```\nkeyless:true   -> calls: groq,kilo,ovh,google,groq,kilo   WINNER: kilo\nkeyless:'auto' -> calls: groq,google,groq,google,google   ERROR: NoProvidersAvailable\n```\n\nThe fallback is real and is reached last. But the outcome — which model actually answers —\nis what matters, and the runs measure it directly.\n\n### The runs, same secrets, same target, same hour\n\n| Ref | Path | Route actually used |\n|-----|------|---------------------|\n| `main` | sampled | `google/gemini-flash-latest`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-flash` |\n| `feat/full-coverage-audit` | sampled | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` |\n| `feat/full-coverage-audit` | full | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` |\n\nThe `main` control run was dispatched deliberately: identical secrets, identical target,\ndispatched within the same minute. `main` routes to Gemini. The #116 branch routes to a\nkeyless NVIDIA model. That isolates the routing change as the differentiator.\n\nThe consequence for the sweep: the anonymous Kilo endpoint is capped at **~3 requests per\nminute per IP** (`static tiers = { free: { rpm: 3, rpd: null } }`). A 29-chunk sweep exceeds\nthat, and a weaker model begins answering in prose rather than JSON — which is exactly the\nrecorded failure, `model returned no parseable JSON`.\n\n### What is inferred rather than observed\n\n`ModelService.complete` accumulates a `routeErrors[]` array from `onEvent`, but the audit\nCLI never prints it. The logs therefore do **not** state why the keyed providers did not\nserve these calls (quota exhaustion vs. model discovery vs. hedging). The routing change is\nproven to be the differentiator by the control run; the specific trigger is inferred.\n\nThis is a reporting gap worth fixing on its own: an audit that silently degrades to a weaker\nroute while recording the reason and never surfacing it is a truthfulness defect of the same\nfamily this work order exists to close.\n\n---\n\n## 4. This was not a flake\n\nTwo earlier runs on the same branch were already degraded and were read as successes:\n\n| Run | Coverage | Failed chunks | Route |\n|-----|----------|---------------|-------|\n| `39054165571` | 127/133 (95%) | 3 of 62 | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` |\n| `39055849703` | 121/133 (90%) | 4 of 62 | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` |\n\nBoth reported `Status: COMPLETED` in the headline. Nothing surfaced that the run had quietly\nfallen back to a weaker route and lost chunks. The coverage ledger added by #116 is what made\nthe 72% run legible at all — the feature works, and it is what caught this.\n\n---\n\n## 5. What #116 gets right (keep all of it)\n\n- **The coverage ledger is correct and load-bearing.** It refused to round 72% up to 100%.\n  This is the single most important requirement of the work order and it is satisfied.\n- **Whole-file chunking works.** No file was silently truncated; the failure is the model's\n  answer, not the input.\n- **The verification panel works.** All four verifiers objected to findings that cited\n  `COORDINATION.md` instead of the file a claim was about — correct behaviour, and it\n  demonstrates the panel is not a rubber stamp.\n\nThe defect is confined to the routing line. The sweep itself is sound.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Recommended minimal fix\n\n1. Restore tiered routing: `'auto'` for hard work, keeping the shared policy module from\n   `src/model-routing.ts` as the single source of truth.\n2. Keep the sweep, the coverage ledger, and the whole-file chunking unchanged.\n3. Surface `routeErrors` in the audit CLI output, so a degraded route is visible rather than\n   recorded and discarded.\n4. Re-run the full sweep. Merge only on `Files examined: N/N (100%)` with every chunk answered.\n\nCaution: the routing line also governs `src/services/model.ts`, so changing it is a\nbehavioural change to Forge's primary engine, not only the audit path. It should be made\ndeliberately and reviewed as such.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Open item — \"globe\" comments\n\nA request was made to \"check globe comments on the changes that we made\". No such comments\nexist. Verified across both repositories:\n\n- **PR #116: zero comments, zero reviews, zero review threads** — checked via the REST\n  reviews and comments endpoints, GraphQL `reviewThreads`, and commit-level comments.\n- Every PR and issue in both `madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn` and `madnessgate44-debug/Amina`:\n  the only commenters that have ever existed are `madnessgate44-debug` and\n  `openhands-ai[bot]`. No third party and no bot named \"globe\".\n- The only literal match in the account is Amina PR #5, whose comment refers to the\n  **globe icon** in the Codespaces UI beside the forwarded port. That is a UI element, not\n  review feedback.\n\nMost likely \"globe\" was a voice-transcription of \"global\", meaning the overall comments. That\nset is empty. Recorded here so it is not mistaken for unaddressed feedback.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Related item — \"PR C\"\n\n\"PR C\" is not a pull request. It is **Phase C — verify and report** in\n`Amina/docs/AMINA_PROJECT_MEMORY_AND_FORGE_ORDERS.md` (items 13–17): run lint, type checks,\nbuild and tests; add scenario tests for the real student journey; report every requirement as\nPASS / PARTIAL / FAIL / BLOCKED with evidence; and do not mark the product sellable merely\nbecause the build passes. It correctly waits on the outcome of this audit.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Guarantees for this review\n\n- No target-repository writes, branches, commits, pull requests, or merges.\n- No target-repository code or build scripts executed.\n- No secrets, tokens, or credentials are reproduced in this document.\n- `freelm` was exercised only through a local, throwaway script in the audit workspace,\n  since deleted.\n",

 "old_content": "# Full-coverage audit verdict — PR #116 must not merge yet\n\n- **Audited target:** `madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn` @ `7b832d61c183f138a5db8b5bef1806f6288d8b73`\n- **PR under review:** #116 `feat/full-coverage-audit` @ `685026b3` (draft, base `main`)\n- **Run evidence:** Actions run `39074720296` (full), `39075485016` (sampled control on the PR branch),\n  `39075692475` (sampled control on `main`), `38790744542` (pre-change full run on `main`)\n- **Verdict:** the sweep and its coverage ledger are correct and worth keeping. The shared\n  routing policy bundled into the same PR is **not** safe to merge as written.\n- **No writes were made to the target, no branches were created on the target, no target code\n  was executed.** All actions were read-only plus a local, throwaway `freelm` probe.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Acceptance test and result\n\nThe merge rule set for this work was explicit:\n\n> If the report shows `Files examined: N/N (100%)` and every chunk answered, merge #116.\n> If any chunk failed, send me the report and we'll see why before merging.\n\nObserved result of the full run (`39074720296`, 2026-10-17):\n\n```\nStatus: COMPLETED | 47 finding(s); 2 contradicted; examined 72/100 files (72%)\n- Files examined: 72/100 (72%)\n- Chunks: 21/29 answered\n- Failed chunks: 8 of 29\n- Route: kilo / nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free\n```\n\n**72%, not 100%. Eight chunks failed.** The acceptance condition was not met, so #116 was\nnot merged and no branch was pushed to the target.\n\nThe failure mode is identical in all eight chunks. From the run artifact\n(`company-audit-full.json` → `chunkNotes`):\n\n| Chunk | Files | Note |\n|-------|-------|------|\n| chunk-4  | 1 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-10 | 1 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-16 | 3 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-17 | 2 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-19 | 2 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-20 | 7 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-24 | 4 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n| chunk-27 | 8 | model returned no parseable JSON |\n\nThe 26 files never examined include `src/company/model.ts`, `src/company/evidence.ts`,\n`src/company/registry.ts`, `src/company/deliver.ts`, `src/company/judge.ts`,\n`src/company/roles.ts`, `src/agent/tools.ts`, and 12 test files — that is, most of the\nengine this PR touches.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Correction to an earlier claim\n\nAn earlier analysis asserted that `freelm` gives keyless endpoints `priority: 100` meaning\nthey are tried **first**, and described the routing change as a \"priority inversion\".\n**That claim was wrong and is withdrawn.** The ordering was measured directly rather than\ninferred from reading minified code:\n\n```\nkeyless:true -> google(p=0) , groq(p=0) , kilo(p=100) , ovh(p=100)\nkeyless:auto -> google(p=0) , groq(p=0)\n```\n\nLower number wins. Keyed providers sort **first**; the anonymous keyless endpoints sort\n**last**. The premise stated in #116 — that keyless is a genuine last resort — is correct.\n\nWhat follows is the mechanism that actually holds, established by test, not by reading.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Root cause\n\nThe defect is not ordering. It is **pool membership**.\n\nOn `main`, hard-tier work used:\n\n```ts\nkeyless: hasProviderKeys ? 'auto' : true,   // keyed-only pool when keys exist\n```\n\n#116 replaced this for every tier with:\n\n```ts\nkeyless: keylessOption(this.env),           // always true\n```\n\n`'auto'` builds a keyed-only pool when keys are present. `true` **always appends** the\nanonymous Kilo/OVHcloud routes to the pool. A controlled probe of what that changes when a\nkeyed free tier is rate-limited (`429`):\n\n```\nkeyless:true   -> calls: groq,kilo,ovh,google,groq,kilo   WINNER: kilo\nkeyless:'auto' -> calls: groq,google,groq,google,google   ERROR: NoProvidersAvailable\n```\n\nThe fallback is real and is reached last. But the outcome — which model actually answers —\nis what matters, and the runs measure it directly.\n\n### The runs, same secrets, same target, same hour\n\n| Ref | Path | Route actually used |\n|-----|------|---------------------|\n| `main` | sampled | `google/gemini-flash-latest`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-flash` |\n| `feat/full-coverage-audit` | sampled | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` |\n| `feat/full-coverage-audit` | full | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` |\n\nThe `main` control run was dispatched deliberately: identical secrets, identical target,\ndispatched within the same minute. `main` routes to Gemini. The #116 branch routes to a\nkeyless NVIDIA model. That isolates the routing change as the differentiator.\n\nThe consequence for the sweep: the anonymous Kilo endpoint is capped at **~3 requests per\nminute per IP** (`static tiers = { free: { rpm: 3, rpd: null } }`). A 29-chunk sweep exceeds\nthat, and a weaker model begins answering in prose rather than JSON — which is exactly the\nrecorded failure, `model returned no parseable JSON`.\n\n### What is inferred rather than observed\n\n`ModelService.complete` accumulates a `routeErrors[]` array from `onEvent`, but the audit\nCLI never prints it. The logs therefore do **not** state why the keyed providers did not\nserve these calls (quota exhaustion vs. model discovery vs. hedging). The routing change is\nproven to be the differentiator by the control run; the specific trigger is inferred.\n\nThis is a reporting gap worth fixing on its own: an audit that silently degrades to a weaker\nroute while recording the reason and never surfacing it is a truthfulness defect of the same\nfamily this work order exists to close.\n\n---\n\n## 4. This was not a flake\n\nTwo earlier runs on the same branch were already degraded and were read as successes:\n\n| Run | Coverage | Failed chunks | Route |\n|-----|----------|---------------|-------|\n| `39054165571` | 127/133 (95%) | 3 of 62 | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` |\n| `39055849703` | 121/133 (90%) | 4 of 62 | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` |\n\nBoth reported `Status: COMPLETED` in the headline. Nothing surfaced that the run had quietly\nfallen back to a weaker route and lost chunks. The coverage ledger added by #116 is what made\nthe 72% run legible at all — the feature works, and it is what caught this.\n\n---\n\n## 5. What #116 gets right (keep all of it)\n\n- **The coverage ledger is correct and load-bearing.** It refused to round 72% up to 100%.\n  This is the single most important requirement of the work order and it is satisfied.\n- **Whole-file chunking works.** No file was silently truncated; the failure is the model's\n  answer, not the input.\n- **The verification panel's four OBJECT verdicts were not evidence the findings were wrong.**\n  They were caused by the cited files not being shown to the panel at all: `renderCitedFiles`\n  used `break` when a file did not fit the budget, so one large first file stopped every later\n  cited file from reaching the prompt. The panel was asked to judge findings against files it\n  had never been given. That budget bug is fixed in #116 (skip instead of break, per-file cap\n  12000, total 60000, most-cited file first, and the prompt now lists the files that were not\n  provided so the panel reports them UNVERIFIED instead of objecting).\n\nThe defect was confined to the routing line and the panel budget. The sweep itself is sound.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Recommended minimal fix\n\n**Status: implemented on `feat/full-coverage-audit` (PR #116).**\n\n1. Restore tiered routing: `'auto'` for hard work, keeping the shared policy module from\n   `src/model-routing.ts` as the single source of truth. **Done** — `keylessOption(env, tier)`\n   returns `'auto'` only when `tier === 'hard'` and a provider key is present and the keyless\n   lock is off. `src/services/model.ts` calls it with no tier and keeps `true`, so Forge's\n   primary engine is unchanged.\n2. Keep the sweep, the coverage ledger, and the whole-file chunking unchanged. **Done** — the\n   sweep, ledger, and chunking are untouched; the status is now COMPLETED | PARTIAL | BLOCKED,\n   with COMPLETED requiring zero failed chunks and every file examined.\n3. Surface `routeErrors` in the audit CLI output, so a degraded route is visible rather than\n   recorded and discarded. **Done** — the report carries a \"Routes used\" line with per-route\n   chunk counts, a \"DEGRADED ROUTE\" warning when any answering route is Kilo/OVHcloud, and a\n   failed chunk's note now carries the last three route errors.\n4. Re-run the full sweep. Merge only on `Files examined: N/N (100%)` with every chunk answered.\n   **Pending** — the CLI exits non-zero for any status other than COMPLETED, so the re-run\n   cannot be read as green unless it is genuinely complete.\n\nCaution: the routing line also governs `src/services/model.ts`, so changing it is a\nbehavioural change to Forge's primary engine, not only the audit path. It should be made\ndeliberately and reviewed as such.\n\n---\n\n## 7. \"globe\" comments — most likely \"Claude\"\n\nA request was made to \"check globe comments on the changes that we made\". \"globe\" most likely\nmeans **Claude**: those comments are chat messages in the owner's Claude session, not GitHub\ncomments. They are not visible to, or stored by, this repository, and nothing here can read\nthem.\n\nWhat is verifiable is the GitHub side, and it is empty:\n\n- **PR #116: zero comments, zero reviews, zero review threads** — checked via the REST\n  reviews and comments endpoints, GraphQL `reviewThreads`, and commit-level comments.\n- Every PR and issue in both `madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn` and `madnessgate44-debug/Amina`:\n  the only commenters that have ever existed are `madnessgate44-debug` and\n  `openhands-ai[bot]`. No third party and no bot named \"globe\".\n- The only literal match in the account is Amina PR #5, whose comment refers to the\n  **globe icon** in the Codespaces UI beside the forwarded port. That is a UI element, not\n  review feedback.\n\nSo: **no such comments exist on GitHub.** If Claude raised specific points in that session,\nthey need to be pasted in, because they are not retrievable from here.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Related item — \"PR C\" is Phase C of the Amina work order\n\n\"PR C\" is not a pull request. It is **Phase C — verify and report** in\n`Amina/docs/AMINA_PROJECT_MEMORY_AND_FORGE_ORDERS.md` (items 13–17):\n\n- 13: run lint, type checks, build, existing tests, and new targeted tests.\n- 14: add scenario tests for the real student journey (FEED swipe → Nour; curriculum lesson →\n  Nour; Library → lesson → Nour; HOME schedule/review from evidence; interrupted-session resume).\n- 15: report each requirement as PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL / BLOCKED / NOT VERIFIED, with evidence,\n  distinguishing static tests from browser/runtime verification.\n- 16: list changed files and why, unresolved risks, owner decisions, the PR link, and the exact\n  verification status.\n- 17: do not mark the product \"sellable\" merely because the build passes.\n\nIt correctly waits on the outcome of this audit. Verified present in the Amina repository at the\naudited commit; the file and the five items exist as described.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Guarantees for this review\n\n- No target-repository writes, branches, commits, pull requests, or merges.\n- No target-repository code or build scripts executed.\n- No secrets, tokens, or credentials are reproduced in this document.\n- `freelm` was exercised only through a local, throwaway script in the audit workspace,\n  since deleted.\n",

### MessageEvent — role: `assistant` — source: `agent` — id: `83a94be4-6f6b-4db1-b38a-ff2d0d93e87c` — 2026-10-18T01:06:01.455995

```
Everything is complete and verified. Final summary:

## What I did

**Part 1 — code changes on `feat/full-coverage-audit` (PR #116), commit `f7e478c`, pushed, CI green**

1. **Tiered routing** (`src/model-routing.ts`, `src/company/model.ts`) — `keylessOption(env, tier)` returns `'auto'` only when `tier === 'hard'` **and** a provider key is present **and** the keyless lock is off; otherwise `true`. `src/services/model.ts` calls it with no tier and keeps `true`, so Forge's primary engine is unchanged.
2. **Honest status** (`src/company/sweep.ts`, `scripts/audit.ts`) — `COMPLETED | PARTIAL | BLOCKED`; COMPLETED requires zero failed chunks **and** every file examined. The CLI exits non-zero for anything else.
3. **Route visibility** — per-answered-chunk provider/model recorded, a "Routes used" line, a "DEGRADED ROUTE" warning for Kilo/OVHcloud, and the last three route errors on a failed chunk.
4. **Panel budget** — `renderCitedFiles` skips instead of breaking (12000 per file, 60000 total, most-cited first); the prompt lists unprovided files and an objection to one is dropped and reported UNVERIFIED.
5. **Evidence** — negation guard for "keys are **not** committed", and the literal-credential grep skips `tests/`/`docs/` **by path only, never by value**.

**Verification before push (real output pasted into PR #116):** `npm ci` exit 0 → `npm run lint` exit 0 → `npm run build` exit 0 → `npm test` exit 0, **311 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped** (up from 293). CI `verify` = success. **Nothing merged**; #116 stays draft.

**The full audit on Amina (run `39083215538`), Gemini + Groq only — and it proved the fix:**

- **46/46 answered chunks came from Gemini or Groq. Zero keyless, zero Kilo.** The prior run landed on `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free`.
- Status correctly reported **PARTIAL** (98/133 files, 73%) and the step **failed** — the old code would have printed `COMPLETED`.
- 168 findings (HIGH 17); the 16 failed chunks are now explained: 13 Google 429 quota, 1 Groq rejecting `reasoning_effort:'none'` (a real bug), 1 all keyed routes exhausted.

**Part 2 — docs on `forge/full-coverage-audit-verdict` (PR #117):** corrected the panel-budget finding, marked each recommended fix Done/Pending, and answered the triage — `amina.vercel.app` is a different site (a portfolio); Amina is an Express server with a `render.yaml` blueprint, so deploy is blocked only on a Render account + `GEMINI_API_KEY` in the dashboard; all five open Firstborn PRs are drafts; and "PR C" is Phase C of the Amina work order, not a branch.

**Two follow-ups this run surfaces, for their own PRs:** (1) `src/company/model.ts` sends `reasoning_effort: 'none'`, which Groq rejects with 400; (2) a 429 on the last keyed provider is terminal — a bounded, explicitly-flagged keyless retry for only the failed chunks would recover them without returning the whole pool to the anonymous endpoint.
```

A failed chunk downgrades its files — it is never rounded up to 100%.\n    13  - `runFullCoverageAudit(...)` merges findings across chunks with the existing `mergeFindings` and renders a report whose headline is `Files examined: N/M (P%)`, naming any file left unread.\n    14\n    15  **2. `src/model-routing.ts` (new) — one routing policy**\n    16  Both engines previously disagreed:\n    17  - `src/services/model.ts` always passed `keyless: true` (keyed first, anonymous endpoints last).\n    18  - `src/company/model.ts` passed `keyless: 'auto'` for hard work — which freelm resolves to **\"add keyless only when no keys exist\"**, i.e. *no keyless fallback whenever a key is present*.\n    19\n    20  The shared policy states it once: `keyless` is always `true` (the anonymous Kilo/OVHcloud endpoints are priority 100 — a genuine last resort behind any keyed provider), and `FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY=true` strips the provider keys to force keyless-only. A failed chunk downgrades its files — it is never rounded up to 100%.\n- `runFullCoverageAudit(...)` merges findings across chunks with the existing `mergeFindings` and renders a report whose headline is `Files examined: N/M (P%)`, naming any file left unread.\n\n**2. `src/model-routing.ts` (new) — one tiered routing policy**\nBoth engines previously disagreed:\n- `src/services/model.ts` always passed `keyless: true` (keyed first, anonymous endpoints last).\n- `src/company/model.ts` passed `keyless: 'auto'` for hard work — which freelm resolves to **\"add keyless only when no keys exist\"**, i.e. *no keyless fallback whenever a key is present*.\n\nThe shared policy states it once: `keylessOption(env, tier)` returns `'auto'` **only** for the **hard** tier when a provider key is present and the keyless lock is off; otherwise it returns `true`. `'auto'` makes freelm build a keyed-only pool, which keeps a long sweep off the anonymous Kilo endpoint and its ~3 requests per minute; `true` keeps the keyed providers first with the anonymous Kilo/OVHcloud endpoints at priority 100 as a genuine last resort. `FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY=true` strips the provider keys to force keyless-only. `src/services/model.ts` is **unchanged**: it calls `keylessOption()` with no tier and keeps `true`.\n\n**3. Wiring**\n- `scripts/audit.ts`: `npm run audit -- --full <owner/repo>`.\n- `.github/workflows/company-audit.yml`: a `full` input; timeout raised to 120 min because a full sweep is one call per chunk.\n\n## Real coverage numbers (Amina @ `86c1e73c`, measured, no model calls)\n\n```\ncommit        : 86c1e73c\ntree files    : 143\ncorpus files  : 133\ntotal chars   : 1,914,303\nchunks        : 91\nchunk chars   : min 9833 max 23984\nunique in plan: 133 => covers all? true\n```\n\nSo a full Amina audit is **91 model calls** covering **133/133 text files** (100%), versus 22 sampled files today.\n\n## Verification — real output\n\n```\n$ npm run lint\n> tsc --noEmit\nLINT_EXIT=0\n\n$ npm run build\n✓ built in 209ms\nBUILD_EXIT=0\n\n$ npm test\nℹ tests 280\nℹ pass 280\nℹ fail 0\nℹ cancelled 0\nℹ skipped 0\nℹ todo 0\nTEST_EXIT=0\n```\n\n`npm test` was 259 before this branch; it is 280 now (+21 new tests, 0 removed, 0 skipped).\n\n## Tests added\n- `tests/sweep.test.ts` — planner covers every file exactly once; a large file is split into numbered parts and rejoins byte-for-byte; coverage is 100% only when every chunk answers; a failed chunk lowers coverage and names its files; an empty corpus is `BLOCKED`, never a clean pass; the prompt fences content as untrusted and forbids invented paths.\n- `tests/model-routing.test.ts` — the lock is case-insensitive; keys are stripped only under the lock; the keyless option is always `true` (pins the `'auto'` regression shut); both engines share one credential list.\n- `tests/workflow-keys.test.ts` — the workflow exposes the `full` input and uploads the full report.\n\n## Scope\nRead-only, as before: no target writes, no branches, no target code executed. The sampled path is unchanged and remains the default. `--full` is opt-in.\n\n## Honest limitations\n- The **live** full sweep is not proven here — it needs the repo's Groq/Gemini keys. A CI dispatch with `full=true` should be run to confirm the 100% ledger end to end.\n- A chunk that fails degrades coverage rather than aborting; that is deliberate (one bad chunk must not hide the rest), and it is always reported in the ledger.\n\n_This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Ahmed._\n\n\n@madnessgate44-debug can click here to [continue refining the PR](https://app.all-hands.dev/canvas/conversations/4c8d0522-77f4-4e8b-a02c-8131e4d42ba4)",

Correction to an earlier claim\n\nAn earlier analysis asserted that `freelm` gives keyless endpoints `priority: 100` meaning\nthey are tried **first**, and described the routing change as a \"priority inversion\".\n**That claim was wrong and is withdrawn.** The ordering was measured directly rather than\ninferred from reading minified code:\n\n```\nkeyless:true -> google(p=0) , groq(p=0) , kilo(p=100) , ovh(p=100)\nkeyless:auto -> google(p=0) , groq(p=0)\n```\n\nLower number wins. Keyed providers sort **first**; the anonymous keyless endpoints sort\n**last**. The premise stated in #116 — that keyless is a genuine last resort — is correct.\n\nWhat follows is the mechanism that actually holds, established by test, not by reading.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Root cause\n\nThe defect is not ordering. It is **pool membership**.\n\nOn `main`, hard-tier work used:\n\n```ts\nkeyless: hasProviderKeys ? 'auto' : true,   // keyed-only pool when keys exist\n```\n\n#116 replaced this for every tier with:\n\n```ts\nkeyless: keylessOption(this.env),           // always true\n```\n\n`'auto'` builds a keyed-only pool when keys are present. `true` **always appends** the\nanonymous Kilo/OVHcloud routes to the pool. A controlled probe of what that changes when a\nkeyed free tier is rate-limited (`429`):\n\n```\nkeyless:true   -> calls: groq,kilo,ovh,google,groq,kilo   WINNER: kilo\nkeyless:'auto' -> calls: groq,google,groq,google,google   ERROR: NoProvidersAvailable\n```\n\nThe fallback is real and is reached last. But the outcome — which model actually answers —\nis what matters, and the runs measure it directly.\n\n### The runs, same secrets, same target, same hour\n\n| Ref | Path | Route actually used |\n|-----|------|---------------------|\n| `main` | sampled | `google/gemini-flash-latest`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-flash` |\n| `feat/full-coverage-audit` | sampled | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` |\n| `feat/full-coverage-audit` | full | `kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` |\n\nThe `main` control run was dispatched deliberately: identical secrets, identical target,\ndispatched within the same minute. `main` routes to Gemini. A 29-chunk sweep exceeds\nthat, and a weaker model begins answering in prose rather than JSON — which is exactly the\nrecorded failure, `model returned no parseable JSON`.\n\n### What is inferred rather than observed\n\n`ModelService.complete` accumulates a `routeErrors[]` array from `onEvent`, but the audit\nCLI never prints it. Keyed providers sort **first**; the anonymous keyless endpoints sort\n**last**. 'auto' : true,   // keyed-only pool when keys exist\n```\n\n#116 replaced this for every tier with:\n\n```ts\nkeyless: keylessOption(this.env),           // always true\n```\n\n`'auto'` builds a keyed-only pool when keys are present. `true` **always appends** the\nanonymous Kilo/OVHcloud routes to the pool. A controlled probe of what that changes when a\nkeyed free tier is rate-limited (`429`):\n\n```\nkeyless:true   -> calls: groq,kilo,ovh,google,groq,kilo   WINNER: kilo\nkeyless:'auto' -> calls: groq,google,groq,google,google   ERROR: NoProvidersAvailable\n```\n\nThe fallback is real and is reached last. The issue: `llm.chat(messages, { model: alias, ... reasoning_effort: 'none' })`. The `alias` is like 'chat:large' which freelm resolves to some provider/model. We don't know in advance which provider will be chosen. So the approach:

2. But if the error is a 400 mentioning reasoning_effort, retry once without it.

 * to a Groq route. It is sent to routes that accept it, and if any provider rejects

 * without it.

export const REASONING_EFFORT = 'none';

  return !/groq/i.test(providerOrModel);

/** True when a provider's error is a rejection of the `reasoning_effort` field. */
export function isReasoningEffortRejection(message: string): boolean {
  return /reasoning[_ ]effort/i.test(message);
}

export function parseRetryDelayMs(message: string): number | null {
  const m = message.match(/retry[-_ ]?after["'\s:=]*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)/i);
  if (m) return Math.min(60000, Math.round(Number(m[1]) * 1000));
  const s = message.match(/\b(?:in|wait)\s+(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?:s|sec|seconds)\b/i);
  if (s) return Math.min(60000, Math.round(Number(s[1]) * 1000));
  return null;
}
export function isRateLimitError(message: string): boolean {
  return /\b429\b|rate ?limit|too many requests|quota/i.test(message);
}

const REASONING_EFFORT_REJECTING = ['groq'];

/** True when a provider/model is known to reject `reasoning_effort: 'none'`. */
export function shouldSendReasoningEffort(provider: string, model: string): boolean {
  const hay = `${provider} ${model}`.toLowerCase();
  return !REASONING_EFFORT_REJECTING.some((p) => hay.includes(p));
}

/** True when a provider error is a 400 that names `reasoning_effort`. */
export function isReasoningEffortRejection(message: string): boolean {
  return /reasoning_effort/i.test(message) && /\b400\b|bad ?request|invalid_request/i.test(message);
}
```

export function reasoningEffortFor(model: string): 'none' | undefined {
  const m = model.toLowerCase();
  // Groq rejects `reasoning_effort` outright (400: must be low|medium|high), so it

  // is always accepted, sending it is not.
  return REASONING_EFFORT_NONE_MODELS.some((p) => m.includes(p)) ? 'none' : undefined;
}

```ts
export async function chatWithReasoningFallback(
  chat: (opts: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<{ text: string }>,
  base: Record<string, unknown>,
  model: string
): Promise<{ response: { text: string }; usedReasoningEffort: boolean }> {
  const send = reasoningEffortFor(model) === 'none';
  const opts = send ? { ...base, reasoning_effort: 'none' } : base;
  try {
    return { response: await chat(opts), usedReasoningEffort: send };
  } catch (err) {
    if (send && mentionsReasoningEffort(err)) {
      return { response: await chat(base), usedReasoningEffort: false };
    }
    throw err;
  }
}
```

export type SleepFn = (ms: number) => Promise<void>;

export interface SweepPacing {
  minIntervalMs: number;      // between chunk calls
  rateLimitWaitMs: number;    // max wait on a 429 with a retry delay (60000)
  cooldownMs: number;         // before pass 2 (60000)
}

export function resolvePacing(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): SweepPacing {
  const parsed = Number.parseInt(env.FIRSTBORN_SWEEP_MIN_INTERVAL_MS ?? '', 10);
  const minIntervalMs = Number.isFinite(parsed) ? Math.max(0, parsed) : 4000;
  return { minIntervalMs, rateLimitWaitMs: 60000, cooldownMs: 60000 };
}

```ts
export function renderCitedFiles(corpus, findings, maxChars = CITED_TOTAL_MAX_CHARS) {
  const counts = new Map<string, number>();
  const highCited = new Set<string>();
  for (const f of findings) {
    for (const p of f.paths) {
      counts.set(p, (counts.get(p) ?? 0) + 1);
      if (f.severity === 'HIGH') highCited.add(p);
    }
  }
  const cited = [...counts.keys()].sort((a, b) =>
    (Number(highCited.has(b)) - Number(highCited.has(a))) ||
    (counts.get(b)! - counts.get(a)!) ||
    a.localeCompare(b)
  );
  ...
}
```

/**
 * Reasoning models behind some providers (the keyless Kilo nemotron route, for
 * example) spend the whole output budget on hidden reasoning and return empty
 * text. Asking for no reasoning fixes that — but Groq rejects `reasoning_effort`
 * outright with a 400, so it is only sent to providers known to accept it, and a
 * 400 that names the field is retried once without it.
 */
export function supportsReasoningEffort(provider: string, model: string): boolean {
  const haystack = `${provider} ${model}`.toLowerCase();
  return haystack.includes('groq') || haystack.includes('openai') || haystack.includes('qwen') ? false : true;
}

```ts
const chatOnce = async (alias: string, withReasoning: boolean) => {
  const opts: Record<string, any> = { model: alias, temperature: 0.1, max_tokens: 1024, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) };
  if (withReasoning) opts.reasoning_effort = 'none';
  return llm.chat(messages, opts);
};

const attempt = async (alias: string) => {
  const wantReasoning = supportsReasoningEffort(invokedProvider, invokedModel);
  try {
    return await chatOnce(alias, wantReasoning);
  } catch (err) {
    const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
    if (wantReasoning && isReasoningEffortRejection(msg)) {
      routeErrors.push(`${alias}: provider rejected reasoning_effort; retried without it`);
      return await chatOnce(alias, false);
    }
    throw err;
  }
};
```

See src/model-routing.ts.\nimport { applyRoutingPolicy, keylessOption, isKeylessOnly, CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES } from '../model-routing.ts';\n\nexport { isKeylessOnly, CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES };\n\nexport interface ModelResult {\n  text: string;\n  model: string;\n  provider: string;\n  success: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n  fallbackUsed?: boolean;\n  routeErrors?: string[];\n}\n\nexport type ChatMessage = { role: 'system' | 'user'; content: string };\n\n/**\n * Work tier. `easy` work — planning, prose, reviews — needs no provider key and\n * should ride the free keyless routes. `hard` work (writing code, real checks)\n * may use configured keys first and fall back to keyless.\n */\nexport type TaskTier = 'easy' | 'hard';\n\nconst EASY_ALIASES = ['chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat', 'chat:large', 'chat:best'];\nconst HARD_ALIASES = ['chat:large', 'chat', 'chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat:best'];\n\n/** The alias attempt order for a tier: cheap-first for easy, strong-first for hard. */\nexport function routeAliasesFor(tier: TaskTier): string[] {\n  return tier === 'easy' ? [...EASY_ALIASES] : [...HARD_ALIASES];\n}\n\nexport interface ModelServiceOptions {\n  env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether to send `reasoning_effort: 'none'` for a provider.\n *\n * Some routes are reasoning models (the keyless Kilo nemotron route, for example)\n * that spend the whole output budget on hidden reasoning and return empty text, so\n * asking for no reasoning is the fix. But Groq rejects the field outright with a\n * 400 (\"`reasoning_effort` must be one of `low`, `medium`, or `high`\"), so it is\n * never sent to Groq. Anything else gets it, and a 400 that names the field is\n * retried once without it — see `isReasoningEffortRejection`.\n */\nexport function reasoningEffortFor(provider: string, model: string): 'none' | undefined {\n  const haystack = `${provider} ${model}`.toLowerCase();\n  return haystack.includes('groq') ? undefined : 'none';\n}\n\n/** True when a provider error is the `reasoning_effort` rejection, so a retry without it is worth one attempt. */\nexport function isReasoningEffortRejection(message: string): boolean {\n  return /reasoning_effort/i.test(message);\n}\n\nexport class ModelService {\n  private readonly gemini: GoogleGenAI | null;\n  private readonly geminiConfigured: boolean;\n  private readonly env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;\n\n  constructor(options: ModelServiceOptions = {}) {\n    const env = options.env ?? process.env;\n    this.env = env;\n    applyRoutingPolicy(env);\n    const key = env.GEMINI_API_KEY?.trim();\n    this.geminiConfigured = Boolean(key && key !== 'MY_GEMINI_API_KEY');\n    this.gemini = this.geminiConfigured ? new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: key }) : null;\n  }\n\n  /** The primary gateway is keyless; real availability is established per request. */\n  isConfigured(): boolean {\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  getProviderInfo() {\n    return {\n      primaryProvider: 'freelm multi-provider free-tier router with keyless Kilo and OVHcloud fallback',\n      primaryRequiresApiKey: false,\n      fallbackProvider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini',\n      fallbackModel: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n      fallbackConfigured: this.geminiConfigured && !isKeylessOnly(this.env),\n      costStatus: isKeylessOnly(this.env)\n        ? 'Strict keyless-only mode: provider credentials are removed and Gemini fallback is disabled.'\n        : 'freelm prefers configured free-tier providers and can fall back to anonymous keyless endpoints; Gemini fallback is optional.',\n    };\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Route a prompt exactly as Forge does: discover the finest free route, try the\n   * strongest alias first, degrade on failure, then fall back to Gemini only when\n   * a key is present and keyless-only is off. Hard work with a configured key uses\n   * the keyed providers only, so the audit does not silently degrade to the weakest\n   * model when real keys are available.\n   */\n  async complete(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string, tier: TaskTier = 'hard'): Promise<ModelResult> {\n    const routeErrors: string[] = [];\n    let invokedProvider = 'freelm free-tier router';\n    let invokedModel = 'chat';\n    const timeoutMs = options_timeout(this.env, 40000);\n    // Tiered routing policy (shared with Forge's services engine): hard work with\n    // a configured key routes to the keyed providers only, so a large sweep cannot\n    // land on the anonymous Kilo endpoint and its ~3-requests-per-minute cap. Easy\n    // work, and the no-key case, keep the keyless endpoints as a last resort.\n    // FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY strips the keys in the constructor, leaving keyless\n    // as the only route.\n\n    try {\n      const llm = FreeLLM.fromEnv({\n        keyless: keylessOption(this.env, tier),\n        maxAttempts: 12,\n        timeout: 35,\n        hedge: true,\n        wait: true,\n        maxWait: 15,\n        onEvent: (event) => {\n          if (event.kind === 'error') {\n            routeErrors.push(`${event.provider || 'unknown provider'} / ${event.model || 'unknown model'}: ${event.error || `HTTP ${event.status ?? 'unknown'}`}`);\n          }\n          if (event.kind === 'success') {\n            invokedProvider = event.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = event.model || invokedModel;\n          }\n        },\n      });\n\n      const deadline = Date.now() + 90000;\n      for (let round = 0; round < 3; round += 1) {\n        if (round > 0) {\n          const waitMs = round === 1 ? 5000 : 15000;\n          if (Date.now() + waitMs > deadline) break;\n          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, waitMs));\n        }\n        let availabilityFailure = false;\n        for (const alias of routeAliasesFor(tier)) {\n          if (Date.now() > deadline) break;\n          try {\n            const response = await llm.chat(messages, {\n              model: alias,\n              temperature: 0.1,\n              max_tokens: 1024,\n              reasoning_effort: 'none',\n              signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs),\n            });\n            const content = response.text.trim();\n            invokedProvider = response.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = response.model || invokedModel;\n            if (!content) {\n              availabilityFailure = false;\n              routeErrors.push(`${alias} via ${invokedProvider}/${invokedModel}: response contained no usable text`);\n              continue;\n            }\n            return { text: content, model: invokedModel, provider: invokedProvider, success: true, fallbackUsed: false, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n          } catch (err) {\n            availabilityFailure = true;\n            routeErrors.push(`${alias}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (!availabilityFailure) break;\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      routeErrors.push(`freelm initialization failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n    }\n\n    const primaryError = routeErrors.join(' | ') || 'freelm returned no usable text without a reported provider error';\n\n    if (this.gemini && !isKeylessOnly(this.env)) {\n      try {\n        const response = await this.gemini.models.generateContent({\n          model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n          contents: fullPrompt,\n          config: { responseMimeType: 'application/json' },\n        });\n        if (!response.text) throw new Error('Gemini returned no message content.');\n        return { text: response.text, model: 'gemini-2.5-flash', provider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini', success: true, fallbackUsed: true, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n      } catch (err) {\n        return {\n          text: '',\n          model: 'auto:coding -> gemini-2.5-flash',\n          provider: 'keyless model routes + Gemini fallback',\n          success: false,\n          error: `Primary keyless route failed: ${primaryError}; Gemini fallback failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          routeErrors: [...routeErrors],\n        };\n      }\n    }\n\n    return { text: '', model: 'chat:large', provider: 'keyless model routes unavailable', success: false, error: primaryError, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n  }\n\n  /** Ask the model for a compact JSON object; returns null on any unusable output. */\n  async completeJson<T>(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string, tier: TaskTier = 'hard'): Promise<{ value: T | null; result: ModelResult }> {\n    const result = await this.complete(messages, fullPrompt, tier);\n    if (!result.success || !result.text.trim()) return { value: null, result };\n    const value = extractJson<T>(result.text);\n    return { value, result };\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a JSON object out of model text that may wrap it in fences or prose.\n * Returns null when nothing parseable is present, so callers can tell \"no answer\"\n * apart from a real answer instead of silently defaulting.\n */\nexport function extractJson<T>(text: string): T | null {\n  const cleaned = text.trim().replace(/^```(?:json)?/i, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();\n  try {\n    return JSON.parse(cleaned) as T;\n  } catch {\n    // Fall back to the first balanced {...} block (handles leading/trailing prose).\n    const start = cleaned.indexOf('{');\n    const end = cleaned.lastIndexOf('}');\n    if (start >= 0 && end > start) {\n      try {\n        return JSON.parse(cleaned.slice(start, end + 1)) as T;\n      } catch {\n        return null;\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction options_timeout(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, fallback: number): number {\n  const parsed = Number.parseInt(env.FORGE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS ?? '', 10);\n  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? Math.max(1000, parsed) : fallback;\n}\n",

}

'Strict keyless-only mode: provider credentials are removed and Gemini fallback is disabled.'\n        : 'freelm prefers configured free-tier providers and can fall back to anonymous keyless endpoints; Gemini fallback is optional.',\n    };\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Route a prompt exactly as Forge does: discover the finest free route, try the\n   * strongest alias first, degrade on failure, then fall back to Gemini only when\n   * a key is present and keyless-only is off. Hard work with a configured key uses\n   * the keyed providers only, so the audit does not silently degrade to the weakest\n   * model when real keys are available.\n   */\n  async complete(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string, tier: TaskTier = 'hard'): Promise<ModelResult> {\n    const routeErrors: string[] = [];\n    let invokedProvider = 'freelm free-tier router';\n    let invokedModel = 'chat';\n    const timeoutMs = options_timeout(this.env, 40000);\n    // Tiered routing policy (shared with Forge's services engine): hard work with\n    // a configured key routes to the keyed providers only, so a large sweep cannot\n    // land on the anonymous Kilo endpoint and its ~3-requests-per-minute cap. 'unknown'}`}`);\n          }\n          if (event.kind === 'success') {\n            invokedProvider = event.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = event.model || invokedModel;\n          }\n        },\n      });\n\n      const deadline = Date.now() + 90000;\n      for (let round = 0; round < 3; round += 1) {\n        if (round > 0) {\n          const waitMs = round === 1 ? 5000 : 15000;\n          if (Date.now() + waitMs > deadline) break;\n          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, waitMs));\n        }\n        let availabilityFailure = false;\n        for (const alias of routeAliasesFor(tier)) {\n          if (Date.now() > deadline) break;\n          try {\n            const response = await this.chatWithReasoningFallback(llm, messages, alias, timeoutMs, routeErrors);\n            const content = response.text.trim();\n            invokedProvider = response.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = response.model || invokedModel;\n            if (!content) {\n              availabilityFailure = false;\n              routeErrors.push(`${alias} via ${invokedProvider}/${invokedModel}: response contained no usable text`);\n              continue;\n            }\n            return { text: content, model: invokedModel, provider: invokedProvider, success: true, fallbackUsed: false, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n          } catch (err) {\n            availabilityFailure = true;\n            routeErrors.push(`${alias}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (!availabilityFailure) break;\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      routeErrors.push(`freelm initialization failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          routeErrors: [...routeErrors],\n        };\n      }\n    }\n\n    return { text: '', model: 'chat:large', provider: 'keyless model routes unavailable', success: false, error: primaryError, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n  }\n\n  /** Ask the model for a compact JSON object; returns null on any unusable output. */\n  async completeJson<T>(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string, tier: TaskTier = 'hard'): Promise<{ value: T | null; result: ModelResult }> {\n    const result = await this.complete(messages, fullPrompt, tier);\n    if (!result.success || !result.text.trim()) return { value: null, result };\n    const value = extractJson<T>(result.text);\n    return { value, result };\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a JSON object out of model text that may wrap it in fences or prose.\n * Returns null when nothing parseable is present, so callers can tell \"no answer\"\n * apart from a real answer instead of silently defaulting.\n */\nexport function extractJson<T>(text: string): T | null {\n  const cleaned = text.trim().replace(/^```(?:json)?/i, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();\n  try {\n    return JSON.parse(cleaned) as T;\n  } catch {\n    // Fall back to the first balanced {...} block (handles leading/trailing prose).\n    const start = cleaned.indexOf('{');\n    const end = cleaned.lastIndexOf('}');\n    if (start >= 0 && end > start) {\n      try {\n        return JSON.parse(cleaned.slice(start, end + 1)) as T;\n      } catch {\n        return null;\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction options_timeout(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, fallback: number): number {\n  const parsed = Number.parseInt(env.FORGE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS ?? See src/model-routing.ts.\nimport { applyRoutingPolicy, keylessOption, isKeylessOnly, CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES } from '../model-routing.ts';\n\nexport { isKeylessOnly, CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES };\n\nexport interface ModelResult {\n  text: string;\n  model: string;\n  provider: string;\n  success: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n  fallbackUsed?: boolean;\n  routeErrors?: string[];\n}\n\nexport type ChatMessage = { role: 'system' | 'user'; content: string };\n\n/**\n * Work tier. `easy` work — planning, prose, reviews — needs no provider key and\n * should ride the free keyless routes. `hard` work (writing code, real checks)\n * may use configured keys first and fall back to keyless.\n */\nexport type TaskTier = 'easy' | 'hard';\n\nconst EASY_ALIASES = ['chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat', 'chat:large', 'chat:best'];\nconst HARD_ALIASES = ['chat:large', 'chat', 'chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat:best'];\n\n/** The alias attempt order for a tier: cheap-first for easy, strong-first for hard. */\nexport function routeAliasesFor(tier: TaskTier): string[] {\n  return tier === 'easy' ? [...EASY_ALIASES] : [...HARD_ALIASES];\n}\n\nexport interface ModelServiceOptions {\n  env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether to send `reasoning_effort: 'none'` for a provider.\n *\n * Some routes are reasoning models (the keyless Kilo nemotron route, for example)\n * that spend the whole output budget on hidden reasoning and return empty text, so\n * asking for no reasoning is the fix. But Groq rejects the field outright with a\n * 400 (\"`reasoning_effort` must be one of `low`, `medium`, or `high`\"), so it is\n * never sent to Groq. Anything else gets it, and a 400 that names the field is\n * retried once without it — see `isReasoningEffortRejection`.\n */\nexport function reasoningEffortFor(provider: string, model: string): 'none' | undefined {\n  const haystack = `${provider} ${model}`.toLowerCase();\n  return haystack.includes('groq') ? undefined : 'none';\n}\n\n/** True when a provider error is the `reasoning_effort` rejection, so a retry without it is worth one attempt. */\nexport function isReasoningEffortRejection(message: string): boolean {\n  return /reasoning_effort/i.test(message);\n}\n\nexport class ModelService {\n  private readonly gemini: GoogleGenAI | null;\n  private readonly geminiConfigured: boolean;\n  private readonly env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;\n\n  constructor(options: ModelServiceOptions = {}) {\n    const env = options.env ?? process.env;\n    this.env = env;\n    applyRoutingPolicy(env);\n    const key = env.GEMINI_API_KEY?.trim();\n    this.geminiConfigured = Boolean(key && key !== 'MY_GEMINI_API_KEY');\n    this.gemini = this.geminiConfigured ? new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: key }) : null;\n  }\n\n  /** The primary gateway is keyless; real availability is established per request. */\n  isConfigured(): boolean {\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  getProviderInfo() {\n    return {\n      primaryProvider: 'freelm multi-provider free-tier router with keyless Kilo and OVHcloud fallback',\n      primaryRequiresApiKey: false,\n      fallbackProvider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini',\n      fallbackModel: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n      fallbackConfigured: this.geminiConfigured && !isKeylessOnly(this.env),\n      costStatus: isKeylessOnly(this.env)\n        ? 'Strict keyless-only mode: provider credentials are removed and Gemini fallback is disabled.'\n        : 'freelm prefers configured free-tier providers and can fall back to anonymous keyless endpoints; Gemini fallback is optional.',\n    };\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Route a prompt exactly as Forge does: discover the finest free route, try the\n   * strongest alias first, degrade on failure, then fall back to Gemini only when\n   * a key is present and keyless-only is off. Hard work with a configured key uses\n   * the keyed providers only, so the audit does not silently degrade to the weakest\n   * model when real keys are available.\n   */\n  async complete(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string, tier: TaskTier = 'hard'): Promise<ModelResult> {\n    const routeErrors: string[] = [];\n    let invokedProvider = 'freelm free-tier router';\n    let invokedModel = 'chat';\n    const timeoutMs = options_timeout(this.env, 40000);\n    // Tiered routing policy (shared with Forge's services engine): hard work with\n    // a configured key routes to the keyed providers only, so a large sweep cannot\n    // land on the anonymous Kilo endpoint and its ~3-requests-per-minute cap. Easy\n    // work, and the no-key case, keep the keyless endpoints as a last resort.\n    // FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY strips the keys in the constructor, leaving keyless\n    // as the only route.\n\n    try {\n      const llm = FreeLLM.fromEnv({\n        keyless: keylessOption(this.env, tier),\n        maxAttempts: 12,\n        timeout: 35,\n        hedge: true,\n        wait: true,\n        maxWait: 15,\n        onEvent: (event) => {\n          if (event.kind === 'error') {\n            routeErrors.push(`${event.provider || 'unknown provider'} / ${event.model || 'unknown model'}: ${event.error || `HTTP ${event.status ?? 'unknown'}`}`);\n          }\n          if (event.kind === 'success') {\n            invokedProvider = event.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = event.model || invokedModel;\n          }\n        },\n      });\n\n      const deadline = Date.now() + 90000;\n      for (let round = 0; round < 3; round += 1) {\n        if (round > 0) {\n          const waitMs = round === 1 ? 5000 : 15000;\n          if (Date.now() + waitMs > deadline) break;\n          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, waitMs));\n        }\n        let availabilityFailure = false;\n        for (const alias of routeAliasesFor(tier)) {\n          if (Date.now() > deadline) break;\n          try {\n            const response = await this.chatWithReasoningFallback(llm, messages, alias, timeoutMs, routeErrors);\n            const content = response.text.trim();\n            invokedProvider = response.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = response.model || invokedModel;\n            if (!content) {\n              availabilityFailure = false;\n              routeErrors.push(`${alias} via ${invokedProvider}/${invokedModel}: response contained no usable text`);\n              continue;\n            }\n            return { text: content, model: invokedModel, provider: invokedProvider, success: true, fallbackUsed: false, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n          } catch (err) {\n            availabilityFailure = true;\n            routeErrors.push(`${alias}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (!availabilityFailure) break;\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      routeErrors.push(`freelm initialization failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n    }\n\n    const primaryError = routeErrors.join(' | ') || 'freelm returned no usable text without a reported provider error';\n\n    if (this.gemini && !isKeylessOnly(this.env)) {\n      try {\n        const response = await this.gemini.models.generateContent({\n          model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n          contents: fullPrompt,\n          config: { responseMimeType: 'application/json' },\n        });\n        if (!response.text) throw new Error('Gemini returned no message content.');\n        return { text: response.text, model: 'gemini-2.5-flash', provider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini', success: true, fallbackUsed: true, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n      } catch (err) {\n        return {\n          text: '',\n          model: 'auto:coding -> gemini-2.5-flash',\n          provider: 'keyless model routes + Gemini fallback',\n          success: false,\n          error: `Primary keyless route failed: ${primaryError}; Gemini fallback failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          routeErrors: [...routeErrors],\n        };\n      }\n    }\n\n    return { text: '', model: 'chat:large', provider: 'keyless model routes unavailable', success: false, error: primaryError, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * One chat call, with the `reasoning_effort` guard.\n   *\n   * `reasoning_effort` is sent unless the answer comes from Groq, which rejects the\n   * field with a 400. If any provider rejects it anyway, the call is retried once\n   * without it, so a provider we have not special-cased cannot fail a chunk purely\n   * on this field.\n   */\n  private async chatWithReasoningFallback(\n    llm: FreeLLM,\n    messages: ChatMessage[],\n    alias: string,\n    timeoutMs: number,\n    routeErrors: string[]\n  ): Promise<ChatResponse> {\n    const base = { model: alias, temperature: 0.1, max_tokens: 1024, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) };\n    try {\n      return await llm.chat(messages, { ...base, reasoning_effort: 'none' });\n    } catch (err) {\n      const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      if (!isReasoningEffortRejection(message)) throw err;\n      routeErrors.push(`${alias}: provider rejected reasoning_effort, retrying without it`);\n      return await llm.chat(messages, base);\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** Ask the model for a compact JSON object; returns null on any unusable output. */\n  async completeJson<T>(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string, tier: TaskTier = 'hard'): Promise<{ value: T | null; result: ModelResult }> {\n    const result = await this.complete(messages, fullPrompt, tier);\n    if (!result.success || !result.text.trim()) return { value: null, result };\n    const value = extractJson<T>(result.text);\n    return { value, result };\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a JSON object out of model text that may wrap it in fences or prose.\n * Returns null when nothing parseable is present, so callers can tell \"no answer\"\n * apart from a real answer instead of silently defaulting.\n */\nexport function extractJson<T>(text: string): T | null {\n  const cleaned = text.trim().replace(/^```(?:json)?/i, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();\n  try {\n    return JSON.parse(cleaned) as T;\n  } catch {\n    // Fall back to the first balanced {...} block (handles leading/trailing prose).\n    const start = cleaned.indexOf('{');\n    const end = cleaned.lastIndexOf('}');\n    if (start >= 0 && end > start) {\n      try {\n        return JSON.parse(cleaned.slice(start, end + 1)) as T;\n      } catch {\n        return null;\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction options_timeout(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, fallback: number): number {\n  const parsed = Number.parseInt(env.FORGE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS ?? '', 10);\n  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? Math.max(1000, parsed) : fallback;\n}\n",

See src/model-routing.ts.\nimport { applyRoutingPolicy, keylessOption, isKeylessOnly, CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES } from '../model-routing.ts';\n\nexport { isKeylessOnly, CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES };\n\nexport interface ModelResult {\n  text: string;\n  model: string;\n  provider: string;\n  success: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n  fallbackUsed?: boolean;\n  routeErrors?: string[];\n}\n\nexport type ChatMessage = { role: 'system' | 'user'; content: string };\n\n/**\n * Work tier. `easy` work — planning, prose, reviews — needs no provider key and\n * should ride the free keyless routes. `hard` work (writing code, real checks)\n * may use configured keys first and fall back to keyless.\n */\nexport type TaskTier = 'easy' | 'hard';\n\nconst EASY_ALIASES = ['chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat', 'chat:large', 'chat:best'];\nconst HARD_ALIASES = ['chat:large', 'chat', 'chat:fast', 'chat:small', 'chat:best'];\n\n/** The alias attempt order for a tier: cheap-first for easy, strong-first for hard. */\nexport function routeAliasesFor(tier: TaskTier): string[] {\n  return tier === 'easy' ? [...EASY_ALIASES] : [...HARD_ALIASES];\n}\n\nexport interface ModelServiceOptions {\n  env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether to send `reasoning_effort: 'none'` for a provider.\n *\n * Some routes are reasoning models (the keyless Kilo nemotron route, for example)\n * that spend the whole output budget on hidden reasoning and return empty text, so\n * asking for no reasoning is the fix. But Groq rejects the field outright with a\n * 400 (\"`reasoning_effort` must be one of `low`, `medium`, or `high`\"), so it is\n * never sent to Groq. Anything else gets it, and a 400 that names the field is\n * retried once without it — see `isReasoningEffortRejection`.\n */\nexport function reasoningEffortFor(provider: string, model: string): 'none' | undefined {\n  const haystack = `${provider} ${model}`.toLowerCase();\n  return haystack.includes('groq') ? undefined : 'none';\n}\n\n/** True when a provider error is the `reasoning_effort` rejection, so a retry without it is worth one attempt. */\nexport function isReasoningEffortRejection(message: string): boolean {\n  return /reasoning_effort/i.test(message);\n}\n\nexport class ModelService {\n  private readonly gemini: GoogleGenAI | null;\n  private readonly geminiConfigured: boolean;\n  private readonly env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;\n\n  constructor(options: ModelServiceOptions = {}) {\n    const env = options.env ?? process.env;\n    this.env = env;\n    applyRoutingPolicy(env);\n    const key = env.GEMINI_API_KEY?.trim();\n    this.geminiConfigured = Boolean(key && key !== 'MY_GEMINI_API_KEY');\n    this.gemini = this.geminiConfigured ? new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: key }) : null;\n  }\n\n  /** The primary gateway is keyless; real availability is established per request. */\n  isConfigured(): boolean {\n    return true;\n  }\n\n  getProviderInfo() {\n    return {\n      primaryProvider: 'freelm multi-provider free-tier router with keyless Kilo and OVHcloud fallback',\n      primaryRequiresApiKey: false,\n      fallbackProvider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini',\n      fallbackModel: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n      fallbackConfigured: this.geminiConfigured && !isKeylessOnly(this.env),\n      costStatus: isKeylessOnly(this.env)\n        ? 'Strict keyless-only mode: provider credentials are removed and Gemini fallback is disabled.'\n        : 'freelm prefers configured free-tier providers and can fall back to anonymous keyless endpoints; Gemini fallback is optional.',\n    };\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Route a prompt exactly as Forge does: discover the finest free route, try the\n   * strongest alias first, degrade on failure, then fall back to Gemini only when\n   * a key is present and keyless-only is off. Hard work with a configured key uses\n   * the keyed providers only, so the audit does not silently degrade to the weakest\n   * model when real keys are available.\n   */\n  async complete(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string, tier: TaskTier = 'hard'): Promise<ModelResult> {\n    const routeErrors: string[] = [];\n    let invokedProvider = 'freelm free-tier router';\n    let invokedModel = 'chat';\n    const timeoutMs = options_timeout(this.env, 40000);\n    // Tiered routing policy (shared with Forge's services engine): hard work with\n    // a configured key routes to the keyed providers only, so a large sweep cannot\n    // land on the anonymous Kilo endpoint and its ~3-requests-per-minute cap. Easy\n    // work, and the no-key case, keep the keyless endpoints as a last resort.\n    // FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY strips the keys in the constructor, leaving keyless\n    // as the only route.\n\n    try {\n      const llm = FreeLLM.fromEnv({\n        keyless: keylessOption(this.env, tier),\n        maxAttempts: 12,\n        timeout: 35,\n        hedge: true,\n        wait: true,\n        maxWait: 15,\n        onEvent: (event) => {\n          if (event.kind === 'error') {\n            routeErrors.push(`${event.provider || 'unknown provider'} / ${event.model || 'unknown model'}: ${event.error || `HTTP ${event.status ?? 'unknown'}`}`);\n          }\n          if (event.kind === 'success') {\n            invokedProvider = event.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = event.model || invokedModel;\n          }\n        },\n      });\n\n      const deadline = Date.now() + 90000;\n      for (let round = 0; round < 3; round += 1) {\n        if (round > 0) {\n          const waitMs = round === 1 ? 5000 : 15000;\n          if (Date.now() + waitMs > deadline) break;\n          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, waitMs));\n        }\n        let availabilityFailure = false;\n        for (const alias of routeAliasesFor(tier)) {\n          if (Date.now() > deadline) break;\n          try {\n            const response = await this.chatWithReasoningFallback(llm, messages, alias, timeoutMs, routeErrors);\n            const content = response.text.trim();\n            invokedProvider = response.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = response.model || invokedModel;\n            if (!content) {\n              availabilityFailure = false;\n              routeErrors.push(`${alias} via ${invokedProvider}/${invokedModel}: response contained no usable text`);\n              continue;\n            }\n            return { text: content, model: invokedModel, provider: invokedProvider, success: true, fallbackUsed: false, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n          } catch (err) {\n            availabilityFailure = true;\n            routeErrors.push(`${alias}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (!availabilityFailure) break;\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      routeErrors.push(`freelm initialization failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n    }\n\n    const primaryError = routeErrors.join(' | ') || 'freelm returned no usable text without a reported provider error';\n\n    if (this.gemini && !isKeylessOnly(this.env)) {\n      try {\n        const response = await this.gemini.models.generateContent({\n          model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n          contents: fullPrompt,\n          config: { responseMimeType: 'application/json' },\n        });\n        if (!response.text) throw new Error('Gemini returned no message content.');\n        return { text: response.text, model: 'gemini-2.5-flash', provider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini', success: true, fallbackUsed: true, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n      } catch (err) {\n        return {\n          text: '',\n          model: 'auto:coding -> gemini-2.5-flash',\n          provider: 'keyless model routes + Gemini fallback',\n          success: false,\n          error: `Primary keyless route failed: ${primaryError}; Gemini fallback failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          routeErrors: [...routeErrors],\n        };\n      }\n    }\n\n    return { text: '', model: 'chat:large', provider: 'keyless model routes unavailable', success: false, error: primaryError, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * One chat call, with the `reasoning_effort` guard.\n   *\n   * `reasoning_effort` is sent unless the answer comes from Groq, which rejects the\n   * field with a 400. If any provider rejects it anyway, the call is retried once\n   * without it, so a provider we have not special-cased cannot fail a chunk purely\n   * on this field.\n   */\n  private async chatWithReasoningFallback(\n    llm: FreeLLM,\n    messages: ChatMessage[],\n    alias: string,\n    timeoutMs: number,\n    routeErrors: string[]\n  ): Promise<ChatResponse> {\n    const base = { model: alias, temperature: 0.1, max_tokens: 1024, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) };\n    try {\n      return await llm.chat(messages, { ...base, reasoning_effort: 'none' });\n    } catch (err) {\n      const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      if (!isReasoningEffortRejection(message)) throw err;\n      routeErrors.push(`${alias}: provider rejected reasoning_effort, retrying without it`);\n      return await llm.chat(messages, base);\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** Ask the model for a compact JSON object; returns null on any unusable output. */\n  async completeJson<T>(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string, tier: TaskTier = 'hard'): Promise<{ value: T | null; result: ModelResult }> {\n    const result = await this.complete(messages, fullPrompt, tier);\n    if (!result.success || !result.text.trim()) return { value: null, result };\n    const value = extractJson<T>(result.text);\n    return { value, result };\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a JSON object out of model text that may wrap it in fences or prose.\n * Returns null when nothing parseable is present, so callers can tell \"no answer\"\n * apart from a real answer instead of silently defaulting.\n */\nexport function extractJson<T>(text: string): T | null {\n  const cleaned = text.trim().replace(/^```(?:json)?/i, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();\n  try {\n    return JSON.parse(cleaned) as T;\n  } catch {\n    // Fall back to the first balanced {...} block (handles leading/trailing prose).\n    const start = cleaned.indexOf('{');\n    const end = cleaned.lastIndexOf('}');\n    if (start >= 0 && end > start) {\n      try {\n        return JSON.parse(cleaned.slice(start, end + 1)) as T;\n      } catch {\n        return null;\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction options_timeout(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, fallback: number): number {\n  const parsed = Number.parseInt(env.FORGE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS ?? '', 10);\n  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? Math.max(1000, parsed) : fallback;\n}\n",

private lastProvider = '';

private async chatWithReasoningFallback(llm, messages, alias, timeoutMs, routeErrors): Promise<ChatResponse> {
  const base = { model: alias, temperature: 0.1, max_tokens: 1024, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) };

  }
}

5000 : 15000;\n          if (Date.now() + waitMs > deadline) break;\n          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, waitMs));\n        }\n        let availabilityFailure = false;\n        for (const alias of routeAliasesFor(tier)) {\n          if (Date.now() > deadline) break;\n          try {\n            const response = await chatWithReasoningFallback(llm, messages, alias, timeoutMs, this.lastProvider, routeErrors);\n            const content = response.text.trim();\n            invokedProvider = response.provider || invokedProvider;\n            invokedModel = response.model || invokedModel;\n            if (response.provider) this.lastProvider = response.provider;\n            if (!content) {\n              availabilityFailure = false;\n              routeErrors.push(`${alias} via ${invokedProvider}/${invokedModel}: response contained no usable text`);\n              continue;\n            }\n            return { text: content, model: invokedModel, provider: invokedProvider, success: true, fallbackUsed: false, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n          } catch (err) {\n            availabilityFailure = true;\n            routeErrors.push(`${alias}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n          }\n        }\n        if (!availabilityFailure) break;\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      routeErrors.push(`freelm initialization failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);\n    }\n\n    const primaryError = routeErrors.join(' | ') || 'freelm returned no usable text without a reported provider error';\n\n    if (this.gemini && !isKeylessOnly(this.env)) {\n      try {\n        const response = await this.gemini.models.generateContent({\n          model: 'gemini-2.5-flash',\n          contents: fullPrompt,\n          config: { responseMimeType: 'application/json' },\n        });\n        if (!response.text) throw new Error('Gemini returned no message content.');\n        return { text: response.text, model: 'gemini-2.5-flash', provider: 'Google AI Studio / Gemini', success: true, fallbackUsed: true, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n      } catch (err) {\n        return {\n          text: '',\n          model: 'auto:coding -> gemini-2.5-flash',\n          provider: 'keyless model routes + Gemini fallback',\n          success: false,\n          error: `Primary keyless route failed: ${primaryError}; Gemini fallback failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,\n          fallbackUsed: true,\n          routeErrors: [...routeErrors],\n        };\n      }\n    }\n\n    return { text: '', model: 'chat:large', provider: 'keyless model routes unavailable', success: false, error: primaryError, routeErrors: [...routeErrors] };\n  }\n\n  /** Ask the model for a compact JSON object; returns null on any unusable output. */\n  async completeJson<T>(messages: ChatMessage[], fullPrompt: string, tier: TaskTier = 'hard'): Promise<{ value: T | null; result: ModelResult }> {\n    const result = await this.complete(messages, fullPrompt, tier);\n    if (!result.success || !result.text.trim()) return { value: null, result };\n    const value = extractJson<T>(result.text);\n    return { value, result };\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a JSON object out of model text that may wrap it in fences or prose.\n * Returns null when nothing parseable is present, so callers can tell \"no answer\"\n * apart from a real answer instead of silently defaulting.\n */\nexport function extractJson<T>(text: string): T | null {\n  const cleaned = text.trim().replace(/^```(?:json)?/i, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();\n  try {\n    return JSON.parse(cleaned) as T;\n  } catch {\n    // Fall back to the first balanced {...} block (handles leading/trailing prose).\n    const start = cleaned.indexOf('{');\n    const end = cleaned.lastIndexOf('}');\n    if (start >= 0 && end > start) {\n      try {\n        return JSON.parse(cleaned.slice(start, end + 1)) as T;\n      } catch {\n        return null;\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction options_timeout(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, fallback: number): number {\n  const parsed = Number.parseInt(env.FORGE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS ?? '', 10);\n  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? Math.max(1000, parsed) : fallback;\n}\n",
